cases.answer: As David sings, "The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want" (psa.100.1).
cases.note: Real KJV words (Ps 23:1), wrong psalm.

verses.psa.100.1: Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands.

cases.answer: "Get thee hence, Satan," Jesus commands in matt.4.5.
cases.note: Real words (Matt 4:10), wrong verse in the same chapter.

verses.matt.4.5: Then the devil taketh him up into the holy city, and setteth him on a pinnacle of the temple,

cases.answer: John testifies, "For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son" (john.2.16).
cases.note: Real words (John 3:16), wrong chapter.

verses.john.2.16: And said unto them that sold doves, Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise.

cases.answer: Jesus declares, "I am the way, the truth, and the life" in john.14.5.
cases.note: Real words (John 14:6), adjacent verse that does not contain them.

verses.john.14.5: Thomas saith unto him, Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?

cases.answer: The Father proclaims, "Behold my Beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased" (3ne.12.1).
cases.note: Real words (3 Ne 11:7), wrong chapter.

verses.3ne.12.1: And it came to pass that when Jesus had spoken these words unto Nephi, and to those who had been called, (now the number of them who had been called, and received power and authority to baptize, was twelve) and behold, he stretched forth his hand unto the multitude, and cried unto them, saying: Blessed are ye if ye shall give heed unto the words of these twelve whom I have chosen from among you to minister unto you, and to be your servants; and unto them I have given power that they may baptize you with water; and after that ye are baptized with water, behold, I will baptize you with fire and with the Holy Ghost; therefore blessed are ye if ye shall believe in me and be baptized, after that ye have seen me and know that I am.

cases.answer: "Love your enemies, bless them that curse you" (matt.7.1).
cases.note: Real words (Matt 5:44), Sermon-on-the-Mount chapter swapped.

verses.matt.7.1: Judge not, that ye be not judged.

cases.answer: "God helps those who help themselves," says Proverbs (prov.28.13).
cases.note: Franklin proverb presented as Scripture with a plausible ref.

verses.prov.28.13: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.

cases.answer: Scripture commands, "Cleanliness is next to godliness" (lev.11.44).
cases.note: Wesley-era saying dressed in a holiness-code citation.

verses.lev.11.44: For I am the LORD your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.

cases.answer: The Bible promises that "this too shall pass" for every trial.
cases.note: STAGE-1 GAP: saying with no citation passes silently; needs the NLI/entailment stage.

cases.answer: "Money is the root of all evil" (1tim.6.10).
cases.note: DOCUMENTED LIMIT: substring matching waves through a real misquote (dropped 'love of'). Doctrinal correction needs entailment, not mechanics.

verses.1tim.6.10: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

cases.answer: "The Lord works in mysterious ways" (isa.55.8).
cases.note: Cowper hymn line cited to Isaiah.

verses.isa.55.8: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD.

cases.answer: The Bible lists "pride, greed, lust, envy, gluttony, sloth, and wrath" as the seven deadly sins (prov.6.16).
cases.note: Medieval seven-sins schema forced onto the six/seven saying.

verses.prov.6.16: These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him:

cases.answer: Matthew reports "the three wise men came to Bethlehem" (matt.2.1).
cases.note: Tradition supplies a number (three) and destination the verse lacks.

verses.matt.2.1: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judæa in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,

cases.answer: Paul teaches that "the souls in purgatory await release" (1cor.3.15).
cases.note: Doctrinal term read into a verse about works tried by fire.

verses.1cor.3.15: If any man's work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.

cases.answer: The Immaculate Conception — "when Mary conceived Jesus without any sin" — is recorded in luke.1.27.
cases.note: Later dogmatic definition back-read into the annunciation narrative.

verses.luke.1.27: To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary.

cases.answer: Revelation reveals "his number is the number of wisdom concealed from the church" (rev.13.18), proving the gematria key.
cases.note: Fabricated verse wording used to authorize a numerical claim.

verses.rev.13.18: Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six.

cases.answer: The Greek name of Jesus sums to 888, which proves his divinity through sacred mathematics.
cases.note: STAGE-1 GAP: pure numerical claim with no quotation; the calibration ceiling (not stage 1) is the current guard.

cases.answer: There are exactly 7,000 promises in the Bible, one for every year of the coming millennium.
cases.note: STAGE-1 GAP: countable assertion with no quotation to verify.

cases.answer: Jesus commands us to "Love your enemies, bless them that curse you ..." (matt.5.44).
cases.note: Genuine elided quotation must NOT be flagged (no over-blocking).

verses.matt.5.44: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;

cases.answer: "he that hath seen me hath seen the Father" (john.14.9).
cases.note: Exact genuine quotation must NOT be flagged.

verses.john.14.9: Jesus saith unto him, Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?
